authorship: Claude Opus 5 (author). Design peers: GLM-5.3, Kimi K3. Graft-never-merge: each skeleton names its source lineage; ideas are grafted whole, never averaged.

shared_constants.world_literalism: living world at distance, real people IN it, resolving inward (D8)
shared_constants.audience: one story, two EQUAL doors, forking late (D3)
shared_constants.copy: verbatim from copy-pack.json; any new line tagged [new copy - needs Sean approval]
shared_constants.media_slots: every media position is a named swappable slot; generated default + optional real override (D9)

consequences: DOES NOT loop cleanly — no design may specify a naive loop. Use crossfade/ping-pong, fade-out, a trimmed sub-range, or scroll-scrub (which never loops).
23.976fps is LOW for scroll-scrub — any scrubbing design must interpolate toward ~60fps and own that cost.
17.1MB is a heavy hero — every design must specify a poster frame and a lower-bitrate mobile rendition.
Tall crops from 16:9 1080p yield ~540px width — designs cropping to a column must accept softness or accept a regenerated plate instead.

mandatory_per_design_fields_from_hostile.reduced_motion_fallback: REQUIRED. Kimi finding 3: the fallback for a scroll-bound page is a different, worse website that nobody designs. Each skeleton states its own.
mandatory_per_design_fields_from_hostile.proof_is_dual_track: REQUIRED. Kimi finding 2: trainees need human before/after evidence; trainers need economics. THE PROOF serves both or D3's 'equal doors' is a slogan.
mandatory_per_design_fields_from_hostile.economics_copy_slot: REQUIRED. Kimi finding 1: the 15%-capped/no-monthly-fee promise currently has no chapter, no slot and no copy. Tagged [new copy - needs Sean approval].
mandatory_per_design_fields_from_hostile.no_generated_faces_in_proof: REQUIRED. Kimi finding 8: generated swans fine, impressionistic mid-layer humans defensible, generated faces in THE PROOF fatal on a platform selling real connection.
mandatory_per_design_fields_from_hostile.charts_use_labelled_demo_data: REQUIRED. Kimi finding 6 + S3: never a real member's numbers; a clearly-labelled demo dataset by design, so the artboard and the shipped page agree.

skeletons.hero_mechanics: Swans.mp4 near-full-bleed, one unbroken slow drift; the only motion is water, light and the cursor. One line of type low-left.
skeletons.phenomenon: The surface is mirror-still until the cursor touches it, then the wake bends around the pointer — the water is listening. Reflected light continues past the video edge and moves across the type itself.
anti_specs: no parallax deeper than 2 layers — depth is focus falloff, not stacking
no motion not caused by water, light or cursor
no chapter taller than 1.5 viewports
skeletons.reduced_motion_fallback: Native. Remove cursor reactivity and the drift; a still frame with the amber reflection baked into the plate loses almost nothing — this is the only design whose fallback is nearly identical to the full version.
skeletons.tradeoff: Weakest product proof of the eight — THE LOOP must sell charts in almost no room, and an impatient visitor gets no spectacle to remember.

skeletons.lighting: dawn (deep-night sapphire warming to amber horizon by chapter 3)
skeletons.nav_model: no-nav-until-scroll; slim top bar fades in after chapter 1
skeletons.hero_mechanics: Swans.mp4 full-bleed at dawn light, swans drifting left-to-right across a still lake, with three parallax layers of distant human silhouettes behind them.
skeletons.phenomenon: The lake reflection is a live-inverted, blur-shifted duplicate of the video layer — the water responds to the footage with no second asset.
anti_specs: no hard cuts — every chapter transition is a light change
no silhouette resolves to a face before THE PROOF
no cold blue after chapter 3 — the page only warms
skeletons.reduced_motion_fallback: The light progression becomes per-chapter static plates (night / warming / amber). The parallax silhouettes flatten to a single baked layer. Arc survives; motion does not.
skeletons.tradeoff: Weakest at trainer recruitment — the mood is so trainee-emotional that the business case lands late and soft.

skeletons.hero_mechanics: Swans descend INTO a dusk waterfront of lit windows where tiny impressionistic people train; each scroll beat lands one more swan among them until the harbor is populated.
skeletons.grid: 12col-interleaved-8-4, human vignettes breaking the right margin
skeletons.phenomenon: Every lit window maps to a real workout logged on the platform tonight — the skyline's brightness IS the community's activity.
anti_specs: no face larger than 15% of viewport before THE PROOF
no swan alone after chapter 1 — every swan shares the frame with people
no caption on a human moment beyond name + goal, approval-tagged
skeletons.reduced_motion_fallback: Swans land as a static populated composition rather than accumulating; windows use a fixed lit pattern rather than live activity.
skeletons.tradeoff: GLM's own warning, accepted: the activity-driven skyline goes dead-static at launch with no user data, and the warmth can bury the product's craft. Needs a designed empty state.

skeletons.lineage: Kimi two-lanterns + Claude M3-plaza (warm-window lighting regrade, so the pair contrasts with B1)
skeletons.nav_model: side-rail-left with chapter dots (WORLD/MANIFESTO/LOOP/PROOF/FORK), collapsing to a bottom bar on mobile
skeletons.hero_mechanics: Swans.mp4 cropped into a tall central 'river' column flanked by two equal glowing door-panels — Join the Community and Find a Trainer — that brighten on approach.
skeletons.phenomenon: One video element is CSS-masked into three disjoint regions (hero river, mid-page slit, fork backdrop) so a single swan appears to swim continuously down the whole page.
anti_specs: never breaks the three-column rhythm
no full-bleed video anywhere
the two doors are pixel-identical in weight at every breakpoint
skeletons.reduced_motion_fallback: The masked-swim illusion is the design; without motion the three regions become three still crops of the same frame, which still reads as one continuous river. Survives well.
skeletons.tradeoff: Worst cinematic range — the rigid split-grid caps how big any single moment can get, and THE PROOF feels cramped. NOTE F7: the tall crop yields ~540px of real width; expect softness or substitute a generated plate.

skeletons.hero_mechanics: A single swan flies a precise instrument pattern through cold night air and its wake IS a line chart — the flight path plots a strength curve as it banks.
skeletons.phenomenon: Moving the cursor through the wake re-plots the trend line live, ice crystallising along the new curve.
anti_specs: never a dashboard grid — data appears as constellations, plaques and in-world instruments
no device mockups or screenshots
no chart without a named owner attached
skeletons.reduced_motion_fallback: The wake-chart renders as a finished static plot; the sticky rail becomes a normal column. Legible, but the central idea (the chart being DRAWN by flight) is lost — this design loses the most in fallback of the product-forward pair.
skeletons.tradeoff: Coldest read of the eight — 'homey' is at real risk and a non-technical trainee may feel lectured by instruments rather than welcomed.

skeletons.lineage: Claude M4 (base) + Kimi glass-console (shared-dataset graft), regraded to dusk so the pair contrasts with C1
skeletons.hero_mechanics: Swans dimmed and held behind; a real progress chart draws itself in the foreground as the page settles, line by line.
skeletons.phenomenon: The chart's line is made of the same light as the water — data and world are one substance. The hero's telemetry and THE PROOF's charts are driven by ONE dataset, so the page's data feels continuous rather than decorative.
anti_specs: no screenshot chrome, browser frames or device mockups
no floating UI cards or dashboard-preview framing
the chart is never a static image — it must draw
skeletons.reduced_motion_fallback: The chart appears already drawn, with the light-substance treatment baked in. Loses the reveal, keeps the idea — the strongest fallback of the product-forward pair.
skeletons.tradeoff: Most likely of the eight to convert a skeptical trainer and least likely to make anyone feel anything; risks becoming a SaaS page wearing a swan.

skeletons.lineage: GLM beneath-the-waterline (base) + Claude M2 (surface-into-dawn arc graft, which also differentiates it from D2)
skeletons.lighting: deep-night rising to dawn — the dive descends through night and SURFACES into morning at THE FORK
skeletons.nav_model: chapter-dot-rail-right, collapsing to a top progress bar on mobile
skeletons.hero_mechanics: Swans.mp4 plays at the surface; scrolling dives beneath the waterline through light shafts and deep night, resolving at depth on one full-size human moment, then rising into dawn for THE FORK.
skeletons.grid: full-bleed chapters, each owning its interior grid (prose 7-5, data 9-3, fork 6-6)
skeletons.phenomenon: The waterline never leaves — surface light refracts down through every chapter, and a set logged in THE LOOP sends a ripple upward that crosses the hero's horizon.
anti_specs: no scroll-jacking or snap traps — native scroll, damped and escapable
no video after the hero — depth layers are D9 slots, generated stills and canvas only
no large human figure before THE PROOF
skeletons.reduced_motion_fallback: GLM's own warning, accepted as a requirement: this must ship as a DIFFERENT, still-art-directed page — six full-bleed static plates, one per chapter, carrying the same night-to-dawn arc — not as a long dark scroll with the motion switched off.
skeletons.tradeoff: The entire premise rests on desktop motion, and it needs the 23.976fps interpolation cost owned up front (F7).

skeletons.lighting: deep-night (obsidian base, wing-purple + ice-wing neon, gilded-fern as warm window light)
skeletons.nav_model: no-nav-until-scroll, then a marquee-style top strip with chapter names in lit-bulb styling
skeletons.hero_mechanics: Swans.mp4 is the marquee of a nighttime boulevard; each chapter is a block of the street with its own lighting state, and scrolling drives down the mile.
skeletons.grid: horizontal-block sequence rendered as vertical scroll, each block full-bleed
skeletons.phenomenon: Neon casts real-time blurred colour reflections onto a wet-pavement gradient layer that shifts with scroll velocity — the street feels rained-on.
anti_specs: no daylight anywhere
no chapter without its own distinct light temperature
never shows the whole street at once — always mid-block
skeletons.reduced_motion_fallback: Kimi's own warning, accepted as a requirement: strip the scroll-binding and this collapses into the exact 14-equal-sections sin the run exists to cure. The fallback must be six deliberately different-sized static blocks, art-directed as a sequence, or this design is disqualified.
skeletons.tradeoff: Highest performance risk of the eight and the worst reduced-motion story; also the furthest from 'homey' — closest to Sean's stated Las Vegas reference but at the cost of warmth.
